source.title: A margin-based multiclass generalization bound via geometric complexity
source.authors: Michael Munn; Benoit Dherin; Javier Gonzalvo

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper through its appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains a ResNet-18 on natural and random labels and measures excess risk alongside geometric complexity, providing a conceptual test of whether random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexist and whether a measured property tracks the gap.
record.gate_note: The experiment reports training curves and an explicit relationship between excess risk and geometric complexity. It does not report numeric train/test errors or state that random-label training reached zero error or that natural-label test error was far below chance. Cited findings about width-related double descent and other measures are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures how geometric complexity tracks an accuracy gap during training. A gap alone does not establish V1's random-label fit, natural-label held-out accuracy, or chance-level random-label accuracy. Geometric complexity measures input-Jacobian variability, not V7's tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations. No own results test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report a close empirical association between geometric complexity and excess risk across training in both datasets and label settings. They also derive margin-based generalization bounds involving geometric complexity, assuming a Poincaré inequality and bounded mean model output, and compare empirical with population geometric complexity for Lipschitz functions. They leave assessment of bound vacuity for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The experiment measures excess risk and geometric complexity over training curves; it does not compare the stated architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, width, or memorized-example conditions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and label condition (original versus random) are varied; the text says the correlation appears in both.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-18 trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using original or random labels, the authors report that geometric complexity and excess risk change at comparable rates during training. The figure captions also state that margin normalization neutralizes geometric-complexity growth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-Jacobian geometric complexity tracks the reported training-to-test accuracy difference across training in these settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023 (as stated in supplied text)
record.problems: The experiment is described qualitatively and through figures; no numeric train/test errors, uncertainty estimates, or explicit chance-level test comparison are stated. The paper itself notes that its bound does not reflect width/depth dependence and leaves a detailed analysis of bound vacuity for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported result rows were omitted. Prior-work statements about width-related double descent and other generalization measures were excluded because they are cited findings, not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fit and above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe, with random-label held-out accuracy at chance.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error; the width experiments discussed are cited prior work.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning or recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Effects of adding or removing dropout across data sizes and regularization recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps among low-training-loss networks, and its ranking against norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure text contains captions but no readable numerical curves or separate training and test accuracies. Missing evidence for V1 is not evidence of a partial effect and cannot justify a supports verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No explicit report of perfect random-label fit, chance-level random-label test accuracy, or natural-label test error relative to chance; only the excess-risk curves and their relation to geometric complexity are described.
